tasks.short: Register, code and post supplier invoices and other entries in AFAS, and summarise the ledger.

steps.what: Collect invoices from the AP mailbox and register them in AFAS
Read invoice, key header and lines, find the supplier
Code ledger account, cost centre, site and VAT code

loop.input: Invoice lines with no supplier-history coding rule
loop.output: Proposed ledger account, cost centre and VAT code with a one-line reason
loop.check: Codes must exist in AFAS for the administration; VAT code must fit supplier country and reverse-charge flag; low-confidence proposals go to the queue
loop.stop: One proposal per line, no retries; a failed check leaves the line uncoded for the bookkeeper
loop.why_not_simpler: History rules cover recurring suppliers; free-text lines from new or irregular suppliers need reading.

steps.what: Match to order or receipt and route for approval
Post entries and summarise AP ledger in Excel for the controller

tasks.design: Turn on AFAS Profit's UBL inbox and Scan & herken so invoices arrive as e-invoices, and let AFAS post and approve one-to-one matches with order or receipt. Coding rules come from supplier history; a bounded model step proposes coding only for unknown lines, and approval runs as an AFAS workflow instead of mail. The Excel AP summary becomes a Power BI page on the nightly AFAS extract with touchless share and queue age.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most invoices came as PDFs by mail, approval ran by mail, and coding per administration and VAT exceptions were too varied for fixed rules.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS Profit 8 reads UBL and PDF to line level and posts one-to-one matches; models can suggest coding for free-text lines at low cost.
tasks.still_hard: Touchless shares often disappoint: own ledger accounts, VAT exceptions and PDFs keep exceptions alive, and orders and receipts must be in AFAS for matching to work.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding odd coding, VAT treatment and cost allocations, and answering for the books at audit.

ambition.what: A daily touchless-rate and exception review instead of a monthly clean-up before close.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper works an exception queue and owns coding rules, match tolerances and supplier data instead of keying invoices; they may change coding rules within limits set by the controller.

reach.learn: How unposted and unapproved invoices drive accruals, so the queue is cleared before day one of close.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 reads UBL and PDF invoices to line level and posts and approves one-to-one matches
AFAS Scan & herken turns a PDF into an e-invoice and finds supplier by KvK, VAT number and IBAN
Capture time fell from 2.5 minutes to 45 seconds per invoice with history-based coding suggestions
Booking proposals alone do not give high touchless shares because of own accounts and VAT exceptions

assumptions: Noordhaven runs AFAS Profit 8 or can upgrade
Purchase orders and receipts for most spend are in AFAS
Most invoice volume is from recurring suppliers
unknowns: Monthly invoice volume and share arriving as UBL
Share of spend with a purchase order
Number of administrations and VAT setups across the three sites
research_questions: What share of last quarter's invoices would have been a one-to-one match in AFAS?
How many suppliers can send UBL or Peppol today?
How often does the bookkeeper change a coding that history would have proposed?

tasks.short: Match bank, agency and ledger records, find differences, and report them to controller or supplier.

steps.what: Import Rabobank statements and run AFAS bank matching
Work unmatched bank lines by searching invoices and mail

loop.input: Unmatched bank line with description, IBAN and amount, plus candidate open items
loop.output: Proposed match or split with reason, or 'no match'
loop.check: Amounts must sum exactly or within set tolerance; IBAN must belong to the relation; a person confirms before posting
loop.stop: Top three candidates, one pass; otherwise the line stays in the queue
loop.why_not_simpler: AFAS rules already handle reference, IBAN and amount; what is left has free-text descriptions and partial or combined payments.

steps.what: Check agency invoices against hours and split the g-rekening share
Reconcile AP and AR subledgers to the general ledger and supplier statements
Write up differences and mail controller or supplier

loop.input: Difference record with amounts, documents and history
loop.output: Draft supplier mail or note to controller
loop.check: All amounts and references are copied from the record, not generated; bookkeeper sends
loop.stop: One draft per difference; bookkeeper edits or writes it
loop.why_not_simpler: A template covers the fixed parts; the explanation of each difference varies.

tasks.design: Configure AFAS automatic bank matching on CAMT.053 with set tolerances, and add a bounded model step that proposes matches for the leftover lines. Replace the Excel sheet that ties agency portals to time records with a scheduled Python job on a governed data platform: it matches agency invoice lines to approved hours, computes the g-rekening share and sends only differences to the bookkeeper. Subledger-to-ledger checks run nightly into a Power BI reconciliation page.
tasks.previous_blocker: Three agency portals with different exports, and free-text bank descriptions, kept the work in Excel and by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes small portal integrations and matching jobs cheap to build; AFAS rule matching already covers most bank lines.
tasks.still_hard: Agency portal exports change without notice, and hours approved in the portal may not match internal time records; that dispute needs people.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a difference is an error, a timing issue or a dispute, and talking it through with agencies and the controller.

ambition.what: Check every agency invoice against hours weekly before payment, instead of sampling.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper spends the week on real differences and agency disputes, and decides on tolerances and when to hold an agency payment within limits set by the controller.

reach.task: Flex worker hours and wage tax questions
reach.learn: How agency hours and CAO rates are built, to judge agency invoice differences.

evidence.claim: AFAS matches CAMT.053 lines on reference, IBAN, invoice number and oldest-first sums; misses go to a person
Noordhaven can be held liable for agencies' unpaid wage tax and VAT and limits this by paying part into the g-rekening
AP should run with people on exceptions and every decision logged with its data

assumptions: Agency portals offer hour exports or an API
Approved hours exist in a system Noordhaven controls
A governed data platform is available or can be set up
unknowns: Which time registration system holds flex worker hours
The g-rekening percentage agreed with each agency
Current share of bank lines AFAS matches automatically
research_questions: How many agency invoice lines last quarter differed from approved hours, and by how much?
Can all three agencies give a stable hours export?
What share of bank lines is left unmatched after AFAS rules with a small tolerance?

tasks.short: Calculate and send customer invoices and account statements from contract rates and volumes.

steps.what: Collect billable volumes and contract rates from operations and contracts
Calculate invoice lines in Excel against rate cards
Create and check sales invoices in AFAS
Send invoices by mail or e-invoice

tasks.design: Move rate cards out of Excel into a small governed rate table and pull billable volumes from operations exports with a scheduled job that computes invoice lines and loads them into AFAS as invoice proposals. The bookkeeper approves a batch per customer, AFAS sends PDF or UBL, and AFAS dunning produces statements and reminders that hand over to collections.
tasks.previous_blocker: Volumes came from operations as ad hoc Excel files and customer-specific rates lived in contracts, so calculation stayed manual.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a rate table and volume import cheap to build and test; AFAS already handles invoice runs, e-invoicing and dunning.
tasks.still_hard: Customer contracts with special clauses, surcharges and disputed volumes; the source of operations data is not in the listed systems.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a bill that looks wrong for that customer, and handling credit notes and disputes.

ambition.what: Bill weekly instead of monthly for large warehousing customers, to lower days sales outstanding.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper approves invoice batches and keeps rate cards correct, and may hold or release a customer batch.

reach.learn: Which billing errors cause late payment, to fix them at the source.

evidence.claim: Billing and account status work fits deterministic software with high autonomy
Dutch B2B e-invoicing planned from 1 July 2030, not law yet

assumptions: Billable volumes can be exported from a warehouse or transport system
Rate cards per customer can be written as rules
unknowns: Which system holds billable volumes (WMS, TMS)
Number of customers with non-standard rates
How many credit notes follow billing errors today
research_questions: What share of last quarter's invoices was corrected or credited, and why?
Can operations deliver a daily volume export per customer?
Which customers can receive UBL or Peppol invoices?

tasks.short: Work out costs of materials, services and overhead from quotes and price lists for checks and allocation.

steps.what: Gather quotes and price lists from mail and SharePoint

loop.input: Supplier quote or price list PDF
loop.output: Structured price lines: item, unit, price, validity, supplier
loop.check: Totals recompute from lines; supplier must exist in AFAS; bookkeeper confirms new prices before use
loop.stop: One extraction per document; failed checks go to manual entry
loop.why_not_simpler: Quotes come as varied PDFs and mail text without a fixed layout.

steps.what: Enter prices in Excel cost model and compare to orders and invoices
Allocate overhead to sites and cost centres
Review odd costs and report to controller and FP&A

tasks.design: Build a small price-list app on the governed data platform that stores agreed prices per supplier, filled by a bounded extraction step from quotes with bookkeeper confirmation. A nightly job compares AFAS invoice lines to agreed prices and flags variances, and overhead allocation runs as fixed AFAS allocation keys instead of Excel.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quotes and price lists arrive as unstructured PDFs and mails, so prices never reached a system to compare against.
tasks.enabler_now: Models extract price lines from varied documents reliably enough for a checked loop; a price table and variance job are cheap to build.
tasks.still_hard: Quotes with conditions, volume tiers and indexation; overhead keys are a policy choice of the controller.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a price variance is acceptable and what it means for the cost picture.

ambition.what: A price variance report per supplier for purchasing and site managers each month.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper checks variances rather than typing prices, and flags suppliers above agreed prices for follow-up.

reach.learn: Which cost lines drive forecast misses, so variances are reported in that shape.

evidence.claim: Receipts and cost inputs fit a bounded model step with human checks
Large companies may not agree more than 30 days payment term with small suppliers, relevant when recording quote terms

assumptions: Agreed prices are not already held in AFAS purchase data
Overhead allocation keys are stable per year
unknowns: How many active price agreements and quotes per year
Who sets overhead allocation keys today
research_questions: What share of invoices last quarter deviated from agreed prices?
Are quotes stored in one SharePoint place or spread across mailboxes?
Does the controller want variances per supplier or per site?

role.altitude: The three bookkeepers move from keying and matching to running exception queues and owning match rules, tolerances, coding rules and supplier data, within limits set by the controller.
reach: payroll: flex worker hours and agency wage tax liability
fpa: cost forecast inputs per site
skills_to_grow: Writing and testing matching and coding rules in AFAS
Reading data-quality dashboards in Power BI
Supplier data management including IBAN-name checks
Reviewing model proposals and logging decisions
role.ambitious_version: Most supplier and agency invoices post without touch, every agency invoice is checked against hours before payment, and the team closes the month days faster with a daily exception review instead of a month-end clean-up.
